_comment: Monolith data-driven level layouts (Goldenstone roadmap, Phase 2).
A layout is DATA: this file is the source of truth for what gets placed, not C++.
Built-ins live here (Plugins/Monolith/Config/MonolithLevelLayouts.json).
Your own layouts go in Plugins/Monolith/Saved/Monolith/LevelLayouts/*.json —
same shape, and a layout id defined there overrides a built-in of the same name.
Shape:
layouts.<layout_id>.description   human text
layouts.<layout_id>.folder        outliner folder (default Monolith/Layouts/<layout_id>)
layouts.<layout_id>.origin        [x,y,z] offset added to every entry
layouts.<layout_id>.entries[]     one placed actor each
Entry:
id      REQUIRED, unique inside the layout. This is the identity: re-applying
the layout finds the actor tagged Monolith.LayoutEntry:<id> instead of
spawning a second one.
kind    actor | light | atmosphere | volume. Selects which existing action
places it: mesh.spawn_actor / mesh.place_light / mesh.spawn_atmosphere
/ mesh.spawn_volume.
Every other key is forwarded to that action verbatim, so anything those
actions accept works here (preset, properties, extent, mobility, ...).
'class' is the layout spelling of spawn_actor's 'class_or_mesh'.
'name' / 'label' set the actor label (default '<layout_id>.<entry_id>').
Free-form properties, per kind (all validated before anything is placed):
light       properties           = UPROPERTYs on the light component
atmosphere  properties           = fields of the atmosphere settings struct
actor       properties           = UPROPERTYs on the ACTOR
component_properties = UPROPERTYs on its ROOT COMPONENT
volume      properties           = UPROPERTYs on the volume ACTOR
(spawn_volume's six original snake_case aliases still work and mean
the same properties: damage_per_sec -> DamagePerSec, pain_causing ->
bPainCausing, priority -> Priority, unbound -> bUnbound, blend_radius
-> BlendRadius, blend_weight -> BlendWeight. Prefer the UPROPERTY
spelling in new documents: that is what a capture writes back.)
Apply with mesh.apply_level_layout, inspect with mesh.describe_level_layout,
undo with mesh.remove_level_layout, look at the result with editor.capture_viewport.
The 'readback' section below is the REVERSE direction: it is the allowlist
mesh.capture_level_layout uses when it turns actors already in the level back
into a document. Light and atmosphere entries use the readback sections of
MonolithLightPresets.json / MonolithAtmospherePresets.json instead; only the
generic-actor and post-process-actor knobs live here, because only the layout
system has an opinion about them.
Capture allowlists. Two rules decide what a capture writes: a name must be
listed here (or in the light/atmosphere readback sets), AND its live value
must differ from the object's archetype. Both filters exist so a captured
document stays readable and diffable instead of dumping engine defaults.
'actor' resolves against AActor, 'actor_component' against the root component
(so primitive-only names are simply skipped on a bare USceneComponent root),
'atmosphere_actor' against APostProcessVolume.
'volume_<type>' is the read-back set for a `kind: volume` entry of that type,
resolved against the volume ACTOR class (volume_pain -> APainCausingVolume,
volume_audio -> AAudioVolume). A type with no section here captures no
properties, which is the honest answer for trigger / blocking / kill: nothing
on them is worth restating. There is deliberately no volume_post_process:
a post-process volume already classifies as a `kind: atmosphere` entry (its
settings come from the override bits, its actor knobs from 'atmosphere_actor'),
so such a section would never be read.
AActor::Tags is deliberately ABSENT: apply owns the Monolith.Layout /
Monolith.LayoutEntry tags, and capturing them would make a re-applied actor
fight its own identity. Transform is not listed either — location/rotation/
scale are first-class entry fields, not properties.
Adding a name here changes what future captures record and nothing else;
existing documents keep working. Every name is checked against the real
engine class by Monolith.Mesh.Layouts.CaptureKeysAreValid.

demo_lit_room.description: Three-walled 10x10m grey-box room with a golden-hour sun, sky light, two warm practicals, a window rect light, morning haze, sky atmosphere, a cinematic grade, a movable pedestal that sets UPROPERTYs on both the actor and its component, a doorway trigger volume and an audio volume that sets a UPROPERTY of its own. Reference layout: shows geometry, lights, atmosphere, free-form properties on actors AND volumes, and volumes composing in one document, all values coming from named presets.

three_point_studio.description: Pure lighting layout — no geometry. Classic key / fill / rim rect-light rig plus an overcast sky light for ambient. Drop it on top of whatever is already in the level. Shows a preset being composed with an explicit property override (the fill is the softbox preset dimmed through 'properties').
